searchText: why does overall stake effectiveness seem to be on a downward trend only? https://beaconcha.in/charts/stake_effectiveness The max effective balance is 32 ETH. Without transfers/withdrawals at some point most staked eth will not be used for securing the network so you're saying because the average balance has grown above 32 and isn't being used to secure per say cuz of the maximum dictated the percentage shows as if the effectiveness goes down? Roughly, the numerator equals the number of validators times 32. The denominator equals the number of validators times 33 (or whatever the average balance is, but it's higher than 32) The numerator will stay roughly like that, while the denominator will increase with rewards This would go against the ethos of Ethereum where pseudoanonymity and censorship resistance are desirable features. People can volunteer to be monitored (just like with PoW and operating an Ethereum node), but they should always have a choice to remain pseudoanonymous if they want. I may have misunderstood <@!636289909359116290>'s question, but I though he was referring to have some form of official (whatever that means) seal of quality or vouching for certain pools, or calling the ones that seem like a scam. I have seen some efforts towards this. Beaconcha.in has a somewhat objective list in their site with a classification of pools. The "Due diligence committee" is supposedly studying them and has reports on different pools https://ethddc.org/ but I have some reservations about that project (and I have read many do as well) Ah, I may have misunderstood then. Apologies to re-ask this, but is there a confirmed list of EIPs for inclusion in Altair? Can't see that this obviously exists in the specs repo. Hard to know which ones are scams until withdrawls are enabled There are some things that can be called immediately: if a pool claims to be trustless/non-custodial but requires you to send them the mnemonic, I'd bet that's a scan
